articles.title: OpenAI's $70B Run Rate Meets AI's Infrastructure Challenge
articles.summary: loomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's latest annualized revenue, expected to reach or exceed $70 billion by the end of the year. Plus, Oracle keeps several data centers on track by relying on truck deliveries of natural gas, and a conversation with Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman on the mega AI IPO pipeline and the future of physical AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: From Anthropic to Waymo: Kleiner Perkins Bets on AI’s Next Act
articles.summary: Kleiner Perkins partner Ilya Fushman says AI is still in the early stages of reshaping the economy, with opportunities extending from frontier models like Anthropic to consumer agents, autonomous vehicles and robotics. He discusses why the firm sees physical AI as a potential source of the next trillion-dollar companies, the rapid growth of leading private AI businesses, and why he’s increasingly optimistic about both the IPO and M&A markets. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Buildout is Boom 'Not Bubble,' Says Jared Gross
articles.summary: Credit markets are again becoming jittery over the prospects of more mega debt deals hitting a market already flush with financings to pay for the AI arms race. Jared Gross, Head of Institutional Portfolio Strategy at JPMorgan Asset Management, discusses AI asset allocation and why he believes the AI buildout is indeed a boom, not a bubble. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: We Want to 'Dominate' US: Revolut's Storonsky
articles.summary: Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky lays out the fintech’s ambitions to crack the US market and take on established players including JPMorgan and American Express. He says Revolut plans to build out a full digital banking offer, from credit cards to loans, while using AI and automation to reshape how customers bank. The company is also preparing to test AI agents that can shop and transact on behalf of users. He speaks to Tom Mackenzie at the Wave by Vento tech conference in Turin for the latest episode of Bloomberg Tech: Europe. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI in Banking: Risk and Reward | Bloomberg Tech: Europe 10/9/2026
articles.summary: This episode of Bloomberg Tech: Europe, from the Wave by Vento tech conference in Turin, examines how artificial intelligence is moving deeper into banking. Tom Mackenzie explores how banks are using AI to become faster and more efficient, and the new vulnerabilities that could emerge as the technology takes on more consequential decisions. Guests include JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon, Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky, Evident CEO Alexandra Mousavizadeh and Bending Spoons CEO Luca Ferrari. "Bloomberg Tech: Europe" spotlights the biggest names and trends shaping the region's technology ecosystem as the global competition heats up. This monthly, 30-minute magazine-style show features in-depth interviews with top technology leaders, as well as major investors and policymakers - giving you a compelling A to Z of the most consequential innovations, opportunities and challenges. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: 'Last Night I Had Nightmares' Says Airtel Money CEO Before IPO
articles.summary: Mobile payments firm Airtel Money starts trading on the London Stock Exchange on Friday, a listing that may mark the largest initial public offering for the bourse in five years. How the company trades will be the next test in London’s efforts to revitalize its capital markets. A strong first day would imply the city is fertile ground for IPOs and may encourage more companies to list on the LSE. At the same time, a debut that slips below the offer price would send a negative signal through the market, potentially deterring listing candidates. Airtel Money's CEO Ian Ferrao joined Caroline Heper and Charles Capel on Bloomberg Radio to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus IPO Collapses as AI Valuation Concerns Grow
articles.summary: Firmus abandoned its attempt at one of Australia’s biggest-ever initial public offerings, after the Nvidia-backed data center company failed to lure global investors who’ve grown increasingly skittish over frothy AI valuations. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Who Pays for AI: Financing the Next Investment Cycle
articles.summary: AI is driving one of the largest capital spending cycles in decades, creating new questions around how that investment will be financed and where the risks and opportunities will emerge across credit markets. PIMCO’s Lotfi Karoui, Goldman Sachs’ Amanda Lynam and Barclays’ Brad Rogoff joined Bloomberg’s Romaine Bostick at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Is Set to Postpone IPO, Weigh Private Round
articles.summary: Australian data center company Firmus Grid Ltd. is set to postpone its initial public offering, and the company is weighing a private funding round instead, according to people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Julia Fioretti, Manuel Baigorri and Anthony Hughes

articles.title: OpenAI Investment Boosts Tiger Global's Hedge Fund
articles.summary: OpenAI is in talks to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, with Tiger Global poised for a paper profit of $5 billion. Hema Parmar reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: China’s Manus raises over $500M in first funding round since split with Meta
articles.summary: Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the funding round, and existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund, and others also participated.
articles.author: Kate Park

articles.title: JPMorgan Private Bank Says AI Set to Drive Strong Earnings
articles.summary: Nataliia Lipikhina, head of EMEA equity strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses how artificial intelligence continues to underpin global equity markets, particularly the tech sector. "I think the market comes to realization that actually the AI story continues," she tells Bloomberg Television. "Demand is still really strong, and supply is still constrained," Lipikhina adds. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Isomorphic Labs Seeks Funding at Valuation of $40 Billion
articles.summary: Isomorphic Labs, an AI-powered drug discovery startup spun out of Alphabet Inc.’s Google DeepMind, is in early talks to raise new funds at a valuation of at least $40 billion, according to people familiar with the effort. Bloomberg's Neil Campling has the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Why Investors Are Skeptical Over Australian Data Center Company Firmus's IPO
articles.summary: Nvidia-backed data center company Firmus's IPO, set to be among the biggest listings in Australia, has become "unusually polarizing," Australian portfolio manager Jun Bei Liu of Ten Cap says. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Goldman Says Middle Managers at Risk as New Hires Oversee AI
articles.summary: The newest hires in finance won’t have to wait years to become managers. They’ll be overseeing artificial intelligence agents from the time they join, raising the question of what happens to the current middle managers, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Kevin Sneader.
articles.author: Rthvika Suvarna

articles.title: The Investors Who Bought Anthropic Before the World Understood Its Value
articles.summary: Anthropic had two sets of early investors. One funded it before Claude existed. The other bought in after the company was already well known. In 2021, Jaan Tallinn led a $124M Series A at about a $623M valuation, joined by Dustin Moskovitz, James McClave and Eric Schmidt. There was no product yet, so they were backing the founders and the safety research. In 2024, the FTX bankruptcy estate sold its stake for about $1.3B, against roughly $500M invested, at an $18B valuation. Craig Falls bought 666,667 shares for about $20M. Jesse Leimgruber says his position is up about 5,400%. Two years later, Anthropic raised $65B at a $965B post-money valuation. The 2024 buyers weren't betting that AI would matter. They were betting that a company everyone already called expensive was still badly mispriced. Final returns are still unknown. They depend on dilution, share sales and an eventual IPO.Read All
articles.author: sarahevans

articles.title: Sequoia, Nvidia Back Mecka AI’s Robotics Push
articles.summary: Mecka AI has raised $60 million in Series B funding led by Sequoia Capital, with backing from Nvidia, Microsoft’s M12 and Qualcomm, as it builds technology to help robots understand and operate in the physical world. CEO and cofounder Josh Gao discusses the enormous data challenge facing robotics, how Mecka captures everything from physical interactions to force and pressure, and why scaling physical AI will require major investments across sensors, infrastructure and real-world data collection. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Rising Oil Puts Wall Street on Edge
articles.summary: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." SpaceX looks to raise $40 billion for Nvidia chips, Apple makes a bigger smart-home push with LG, and rising oil and rates cool Wall Street’s record rally. Plus, Apollo’s John Cortese on how the company is pushing to make private credit more transparent. New York Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli joins us on record banker bonuses and how the AI boom is impacting New York's bottom line and Alvarez & Marsal’s Paul Aversano on private credit, record profits and the M&A slowdown. Correction: "This video was edited to correct the spelling of "Paul Aversano" that aired in the program at 10:10 am ET." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: BofA Sees Strong Demand for OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs
articles.summary: Bank of America’s JD Moriarty says public markets have the capacity to absorb massive potential IPOs from companies including OpenAI and Anthropic, pointing to SpaceX’s listing as evidence of strong institutional and retail demand for transformational technology companies. He discusses how abundant private capital has changed the traditional IPO playbook and what the pipeline could mean for tech listings next year. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: SpaceX Seeks $40B for Nvidia Chips as AI Megadeals Loom
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow takes a look at SpaceX in talks with banks and investors to borrow $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia. Plus, Apple plans its entry into the smart home space with a doorbell, thermostat, and other accessories developed with LG; and JD Moriarty, Vice Chair and head of Global Tech Equity Capital Markets at Bank of America Securities, discusses the upcoming mega AI IPO pipeline. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: JPMorgan's Guven Toktamis on Private Equity DPI & Outlook
articles.summary: Pressure to show strong distributed paid-in capital (DPI) is top of mind in the private equity space, says Isik Guven Toktamis, JPMorgan EMEA Head of Private Equity Investment Banking. "2026 has been actually been a good year for sponsored M&A. Overall, M&A volume is up by 40%, and we continue to have a very strong pipeline, of exits," she added. Guven Toktamis spoke with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie at the JPMorgan Tech Stars Conference in London on Oct. 6. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: US venture deal value reaches record $515.8B as exits fail to keep pace
articles.summary: Giant artificial intelligence rounds have pushed U.S. venture capital deal value about 44% past its previous annual record with a quarter still to go, according to the quarterly PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor report released today, but the exits needed to return that money to investors have not kept pace. articles.title: AI computing startup Lambda to raise $4B ahead of planned IPO
articles.summary: Nvidia-backed Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation ahead of a planned 2027 IPO, led by Coatue and Blackstone.
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan

articles.title: Billions Pour Into OpenAI, DeepSeek Ahead of IPOs
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down OpenAI's talks with multiple investors to raise at least $30 billion at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion. Plus, DeepSeek is also close to securing at least $12 billion in funding ahead of its own IPO next year, and JPMorganChase CEO Jamie Dimon weighs in on data centers and AI risks from London's Tech Stars event. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: CFTC, SEC Put 'Some Wind' Into Early VC Stage: Ross
articles.summary: Alex Ross, managing partner of Illuminate Financial, joins Scarlet Fu and Dushyant Shahrawat on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the current climate for crypto venture capital. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: CATL and Tencent back Deepseek's ballooning funding round as the AI startup eyes a 2027 IPO
articles.summary: Deepseek is close to raising at least $12 billion in a new funding round, Bloomberg reports. The article CATL and Tencent back Deepseek's ballooning funding round as the AI startup eyes a 2027 IPO appeared first on The Decoder.
articles.author: Jonathan Kemper

articles.title: Nordic Data Center Group ASP Is Said to Weigh Oslo IPO
articles.summary: AI infrastructure developer ASP Data Center AS is considering an initial public offering in Oslo that could raise the equivalent of about $100 million, according to people familiar with the matter.
articles.author: Pablo Mayo Cerqueiro and Natasha Voase

articles.title: AI to See Massive Adoption 'Unseen' in Previous Tech Cycles, Says Neostellar Principal
articles.summary: American AI companies’ performance lead over China narrowed sharply in past months to a record low after labs such as DeepSeek gained ground, threatening US tech supremacy, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Willy Lee, Principal at Neostellar, offers his view from the VC world when it comes to AI investments and the IPO market. (Source: Bloomberg)
